subject: Whether proving a string absent from the corpus proves the label it names is uncitable
question: Can an absence proof stand while Logic ships the same label spelled slightly differently?

reverify.command: python3 Scripts/logic_canon.py absent strings en 'Input Port:'
reverify.expected: NOT PROVEN, naming `Input Port` to locate
reverify.cost: ~5s; reads committed digest sets, not Logic

method: Took three literals a branch had proved absent across every corpus and asked whether the corpus holds the same label without the punctuation. Then swept all 434 LabelSet literals for a canonical that is absent while a shipped label folds to it.

observations.what: corpora holding a label that folds to it
of those, present in Apple's data
absent from Apple's data but named in an observation record
findings when the fold also folded case
records on main wrongly refused when the fold was a refusal
digests in the committed folded sets

conclusion: No. 'Input Port:' is absent from all 23 corpora and Logic ships 'Input Port', so a colon proves any label uncitable. Three literals were proved absent that way and none had been read off a screen. A second digest set over the same values with decoration removed answers the other half offline. It advises rather than refuses: the fold cannot separate a colon this repository added from a menu's ellipsis, which is macOS convention and which the Korean variant carries too, and folding case as well gave 33 findings of which 3 were real. Made a refusal first, it rejected 7 correct records on main whose strings are a LabelSet's deliberate tolerance variants beside a canonical of 'Autopunch', which is correct and citable.
limits: The fold answers 'something differs from this only by decoration', never 'that is the same label'. Logic's `Set Locators` is a toolbar item and `Set Locators…` is the Navigate menu entry; they fold together and are different elements.

Case is not folded, so a label differing only in capitalisation is not reported. That is deliberate -- runtime matching is case-insensitive -- and it means this cannot see a canonical whose only error is a capital.
The 434 literals are those a LabelSet carries plus bare CJK literals under Sources/ and Scripts/livekit/. A Logic string matched anywhere else in the tree was not swept.
en-US host. The sweep reads committed digest sets over all ten locales, but the worked examples are English.

canon.used_for: the label a branch proved uncitable by typing it with a colon; the worked example this whole change exists for
the canonical beside `Auto Punch` and `Auto-Punch`, which are deliberate tolerance variants -- being absent from Apple's data is the point of them, and refusing them was the first version's mistake
